requirement: R12 refresh ownership, injectable event source, gap/snapshot resync, stale diagnostics

whatExists.injectableFactory: YES in the legacy React client: apps/runtime-ui/app/lib/runtime-api.ts:899-904 defines RuntimeEventSourceLike/RuntimeEventSourceFactory; :2983, :2996, :3016 (subscribeTelemetryStream, subscribeRevisionStream, subscribeRuntimeRefreshStream) accept it and default to new EventSource(url). The new runtime-ui-next Foldkit client has NO event source/subscription: it exposes a manual DiagnosticsRefreshRequested message (apps/runtime-ui-next/src/message.ts:22) and fetches on demand.
whatExists.subscriptionOwner: startDeferredLiveRefresh (apps/runtime-ui/app/lib/live-refresh.ts:6-30) owns exactly one subscription per start and defers connecting until the first load settles. There is NO page-global/process-global owner: app-shell.tsx:214 and route pages (dashboard.tsx:190, observe-activity:86, observe-routing:245, requests:402, router-decisions:51) each call it with subscribeRuntimeRefreshStream, so independent starts are independent owners/sources.
whatExists.gapResync: runtime-refresh-bus.ts:50-61 dedupes revisions <= last per surface and delivers a later revision even when intermediate revisions were missed. The app-shell/dashboard handlers perform a full page reload/route remount on a revision event (app-shell setContentRevision + onEvent()->load; dashboard load(true)), so a later revision after a gap causes a snapshot reload. There is NO explicit gap detector, lastEventId, or resync command; a gap with no later event is invisible.
whatExists.staleDiagnostics: stale-refresh-diagnostics.ts exposes staleChartTitles and StaleChartDiagnostic.staleDataReused; dashboard/observe/requests render a stale-chart notice. The Foldkit diagnostics panel also has a distinct status='stale' rendering (runtime-ui-next diagnostics.ts), already covered by its tests.

whatAdded: Only a 5-test characterization suite (apps/runtime-ui/app/lib/s25a-refresh-ownership.test.ts). No product changes: the event source was already injectable, so no fallback was invented.

proofs.test: fake RuntimeEventSourceFactory is used for subscribeRuntimeRefreshStream; URL asserted; revision event delivered; dispose closes once
two sequential start/stop cycles: exactly one active subscription during each, peak=1, zero after each dispose; dispose twice idempotent
two independent startDeferredLiveRefresh owners open two sources; disposing one leaves the other active (characterizes why there is no single page-global owner today)
proofs.red: intentionally a characterization, not a failing requirement: it records the absence of a global owner

proofs.test: bus delivers revision 1 then 3 (2 missed) to the refresh handler; duplicate 3 is deduped; unsubscribe stops delivery
background chart failure reuses previous response, returns staleChartTitles ['Chart A'], diagnostic has staleDataReused=true

absences: No page/process-global single Refresh subscription; multiple independent owners are possible and tested.
No explicit gap marker, lastEventId, or gap-triggered resync command; the reload-on-later-revision is a handler behavior, not gap detection.
The new Foldkit client (runtime-ui-next) has no injectable event source or refresh subscription at all; only manual diagnostics refresh.

testRuns.command: vitest s25a + live-refresh + runtime-refresh-bus + stale-refresh-diagnostics + runtime-api

unproven: A real EventSource/SSE reconnect and a browser gap with no subsequent event; no product change was made to add gap detection or a global owner.
